We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the SES.3 Level Develop and implement advanced cloud computing environments that align with customer needs and enterprise system strategies, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Identify, troubleshoot, and document complex system and network issues to ensure timely resolution and minimize disruptions. Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant experience. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Additional Qualifications at the SES.3 Level Significant experience managing enterprise cloud environments, including platforms such as AWS, Azure, and hybrid cloud networking. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience with resource provisioning, automation, and infrastructure as management tools, such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Cloud Development Kit, or similar platforms. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. Desired Qualifications Active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. Deep familiarity with hybrid cloud architectures and expert-level proficiency in integrating on-premises environments with cloud platforms in air-gapped environments. Comprehensive knowledge of compliance frameworks, such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FedRAMP, and related standards, with proven experience implementing and maintaining compliance within cloud environments. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons Maintain accurate inventory levels of CNC and HMC tooling, ensuring proper organization and storage. Inspect tooling for wear and determine when resharpening is required, coordinating with the manufacturer as needed. Perform grinding and relief operations on tooling as required. Assemble tooling for CNC and HMC machines as needed. Rework HMC manifold parts as required. Calibrate torque wrenches to ensure accuracy and compliance with standards. Machine and grind fixtures and parts as needed to support production. Operate CNC machines while adhering to blueprint specifications and quality standards. Conduct stability studies on gauges to ensure reliability and precision. Perform initial inspections of parts/tools when required. Support training efforts for manual machining processes. Maintain a clean and organized work while following 5S. Adhere to all safety, sanitation, and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements. Perform additional duties as assigned by the manager. Supervisory Responsibilities None Physical Requirements While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to do the following: Lift and move up to 50 pounds without assistance Able to stand for long periods of time Ability to load/unload machines (requires repetitive lifting and bending) Work Environment Majority of the work time is spent in a manufacturing environment where temperatures are often warm or cool, depending upon the season, and noise level can be moderate to high PPE required as determined by company safety standards: safety glasses, ear plugs, gloves, safety shoes Highschool diploma or equivalent preferred 5 or more years of experience as a toolmaker/machinist Demonstrated ability to setup and troubleshoot tooling issues Ability to assist/develop and or improve processes on new or existing parts with a complete understanding of machining fundamentals and practices Ability to use all relevant measurement equipment Ability to follow written and verbal instructions given in English Ability to meet quality and productivity standards Ability to read blueprints thoroughly Computer skills, intermediate knowledge Microsoft Office Strong attention to detail Ability to work as a part of a team Ability to be at workstation on time, every day unless authorized

Job Description The Social & Design Coordinator for the NBCE Late Night Brand Marketing & Consumer Engagement team will support the creation, production, and execution of social content across all NBCE late‑night shows. The candidate will help concept, design, edit, post, and publish content across TikTok, Instagram, X, YouTube, and Facebook. They should be comfortable working with templates, making quick-turn graphics, drafting copy, and managing the flow of social projects—from intake to delivery to posting. This role will work collaboratively across show teams, the marketing organization, and the social strategy team to ensure content is timely, brand-aligned, and tuned to platform best practices. The ideal candidate has strong creative instincts, a working knowledge of social trends, and the ability to juggle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Flexibility is key, as show schedules and social moments often require off-hours attention. This position reports to the Director of Social & Design under Late Night Brand Marketing & Consumer Engagement. Key Responsibilities Design & Content Creation Design social assets across NBCE late‑night properties for TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, and YouTube. Develop digital branding elements, maintain style guides, and uphold brand standards. Edit static and motion graphics using existing templates; create new templates as needed. Edit short-form videos, including clips, recaps, compilations, and original social-first pieces. Create platform‑native content with an understanding of comedic timing and show voice. Participate in content ideation and brainstorms across shows and platforms. Social Coordination & Publishing Help manage social project workflows, including asset intake, timelines, approvals, and delivery. Draft platform‑specific social copy in show voices. Support on-platform posting and publishing across channels where needed. Monitor social platforms for trends, moments, and opportunities relevant to late-night shows. Collaborate closely with social leads and strategists to align content with insights and goals. Maintain organized asset folders, calendars, and trackers for ongoing content needs. Cross-Team Collaboration Communicate clearly with show producers, talent teams, designers, editors, and internal partners. Partner with show production teams on custom content needs, topical moments, and quick turns. Adapt quickly to last-minute changes, breaking moments, and schedule shifts. Basic Requirements: 1+ years of experience in design, social, or related fields preferred. Proficiency in After Effects, Premiere, Photoshop, and Illustrator. Experience working on a social, digital, GFX, agency, or entertainment team a plus. Working knowledge of TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, and YouTube (including posting workflows & best practices). Experience with photography, video, and audio production. Familiarity with illustration or 3D design a plus. Strong understanding of designing for mobile and social platforms. Ability to write short-form, platform‑native social copy. Organized, detail‑oriented, and able to handle multiple projects at once. Comfortable capturing content or editing on mobile devices when needed. Familiar with on-set etiquette. Additional Requirements: Hybrid : This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. The Company reserves the right to change in-office requirements at any time. This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $50,000- $60,000

Position Purpose: This position is created under the requirements of the River Skimming Program Operations and Maintenance agreement between Veolia and the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District (MMSD). This agreement requires that Veolia provide a certified captain for the District’s river skimming vessel. This is a seasonal, hourly paid position of approximately 1000 hours between April and November. The position will require some scheduled weekend work and other weekly hours may vary depending on weather conditions and situations that occur that affect the The river skimmer boat captain is responsible for the safe and effective operation of the MMSD vessel for the collection of floating debris from the Milwaukee, Menomonee and Kinnickinnic River, the Burnham Shipping Canal, and Milwaukee Estuary as well as areas of the Inner Harbor, as defined in the River Skimmer Agreement with the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage. The position includes the day to day supervision of the crew contracted to staff the boat. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Legal and safe operation of the river skimmer boat at all times. Maintenance of a safe work environment on the boat for the crew and enforcement of safety procedures. Delivery of a daily morning safety briefing. Providing knowledge and training to the crew about rocks, shoals, winds and currents that could damage the boat’s equipment or capsize the boat if not handled properly. Development of a logistical schedule to carry out the services agreed to in the contract. Ensuring that Veolia’s contract agreement with MMSD in regards to quality standards for debris removal on the included waterways are met. Ensuring proper disposal of the collected debris as indicated in the contract agreement. Providing routine maintenance of the boat and promptly reporting of any more major maintenance or repair needs to the Conveyance Dept Manager Promptly reporting any performance problems of crew members to their direct supervisor. Work Environment: This work is performed regularly performed in an outside environment, including in inclement weather. The noise level for this environment is moderate. Education/Experience/Background: High School Diploma/GED is required. At least 3 years of experience operating a small vessel on rivers and inner harbor areas in the Milwaukee area under varied weather conditions. Experience in crew supervision and training. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Skills in safe operations of a trash collection boat under conditions found in the Milwaukee area rivers, estuary, and inner harbor areas. Skills in operating the boat under both normal and unusual weather conditions and river conditions. Skills in responding to emergency situations in terms of crew injury, or boat operations. Skills in day to day supervision and training of boat crew members. Skills in logistical planning for effective scheduling of the boat operations. Willingness to work the assigned hours including on weekends as required. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Courses in boat operations sufficient to obtain and maintain the required licenses and certifications indicated below Possession of the Merchant Mariner Credential (25 ton or larger) Possession of Transportation Workers Identification Credential (TWIC card) Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, the employee will frequently be required to stand, talk, hear, operate a variety of mechanical and electrical equipment, and lift objects up to 50 pounds and heavier objects with mechanical assistance.

Position Purpose: Provides day-to-day maintenance of collection system. Services pump stations as needed. Must have the ability to diagnose basic and routine processes and mechanical problems and take remedial corrective action. Must possess a valid CDL driver’s license and a safe driving record. Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and machine malfunction. Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms. Works in various positions; may work on ladders, catwalks, and supports at heights of 50 feet above the ground. Works with hands extended in front of body up to 40 minutes using hand tools weighing up to 15 pounds. Must be able to lift and carry 60 pounds, in standing and bending positions, distances of 10 feet. Occasional stooping, bending or kneeling and entering confined spaces.

The Associate Director, Statistics provides statitical leadership for clinical development and life-cycle management strategies for assigned projects. Specific areas of work may include clinical trials, patient safety, and global medical affairs. The Associate Diector works in partnership with experts in multiple disciplines to advance medicines to our patients. Responsibilities Provide expertise/lead regulatory submission and product life-cycle management strategy planning and implementation for assigned projects. Provide statistical leadership for design, analysis and reporting for clinical or other scientific research programs. Independently develop protocols and statistical analysis plans (or product safety analysis plans/integrated summary of safety analysis plans/analysis plans for GMA evidence generation). Represent function/department on project team(s) to provide statistical input to compound/drug development and drive alignment with functional management. Partner with other functions (Clinical, Regulatory, Patient Safety, or GMA) to create development strategies for assigned projects. Demonstrate extensive understanding of statistical concepts and methodology. Propose novel statistical methodological approaches to design of scientific studies. Provide sufficient detail to allow programming implementation. Ensure that all statistical analyses specified in scientific protocols and analysis plans are conducted appropriately. Train and mentor staff on statistical methodology and operations. May supervise contract statisticians or junior statisticians. Gain expertise in innovative statistical methods. Assist functional leaders in recruiting qualified personnel and arranging training opportunities for professional development of staff. Develop strategy for data presentation and inference. Ensure appropriate interpretation of statistical deliverables in collaboration with other functions. Collaborate in publication of scientific research. Ensure accuracy and internal consistency of reports and publications, including tables, listings, and figures. Act as the liaison for statistical issues on AbbVie collaborative studies with CROs, academic institutions, government agencies, steering and/or data monitoring committees, joint ventures or licensing collaborators. Build external scientific connections which foster professional development and promote the reputation of the Statistics department. (Clin Stat) Ensure that all applicable regulatory requirements for work processes are met. Critically review regulatory submission documents. Participate in discussions with regulatory agencies as needed. Validate external statistical software to ensure compliance with SOPs and regulatory requirements. (SSG) Lead statistical support for benefit-risk planning and assessment. Provide leadership to the development, delivery and interpretation of safety outputs, including graphics. Partner with cross-functional team to develop output specifications to address both pre-planned safety analyses and ad hoc requests. (SSG) Lead within the Safety Statistics Group to implement strategic initiatives that address processes related to interpreting, monitoring, assessing, and reporting safety data to better characterize the safety profile of AbbVie products, improve efficiencies, and provide greater consistency across therapeutic areas. (GMA Stat) Support or lead GMA Statistics group in partnership with GMA, Clinical Research and Clinical Statistics to develop scientifically appropriate strategies for evidence generation, including GMA studies, presentations, and publications in assigned therapeutic area(s). Support or lead GMA Statistics to provide functional area input for life-cycle management of products. Support or lead communications between assigned product team(s) and functional management. Build/drive cross-functional relationship and collaboration. MS (with 10+ years of experience) or PhD (with 6+ years of experience) in Statistics, Biostatistics, or a highly related field. High degree of technical competence and excellent communication skills, both oral and written Able to identify data or analytical issues, and assist with providing solutions by either applying own skills and knowledge or seeking help from others Able to manage project timeline and quality of deliverables Able to build strong relationship with peers and cross-functional partners to achieve higher performance. Highly motivated to drive innovation by raising the bar and challenging the status quo Have strong leadership skills and experience in working/managing cross-cultural or oversea teams Pharmaceutical or related industry knowledge required, including experience and understanding of drug development and life-cycle management in the regulated environment. (SSG) Experience leading safety-related projects (eg, ISS, benefit-risk assessment, signal detection) (GMA Stat) Competence in experimental and RWE study design, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, statistical modeling, and statistical programming. Knowledge of methodologies for confounding control and bias minimization in observational studies preferred.

The Muliplatform Producer works closely with correspondents to gather all editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, securing interviews, and confirming information with government agencies and community organizations. The successful candidate must excel in a high-energy, focused, small-team environment, be able to initiate and drive new research directions, and have a commitment to high research quality. A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required. Key Responsibilities Lead research, design, and implementation of AI algorithms for computer vision (image and video analysis), multi-modal data and generative systems. Contribute to surgical AI using methods in synthetic data generation, generative modelling, world/diffusion models, etc. Lead development of effective techniques and infrastructure, from the initial idea to the running prototype and product. Contribute to research projects that develop a variety of algorithms and systems in computer vision, robotics, and multi-modal data fusion. Advance the state-of-the-art in the field, including generating patents and publications. Develop validation methods and evaluation metrics to show scalability to large clinical datasets. Contribute to building new clinical datasets and data pipelines. Participate in integration of new ML/CV algorithms into existing and future robotic platforms. Collaborate with users and clinical advisors to iterate prototype designs based on feedback and performance. Develop new technologies and digital products to improve surgeon and team performance on robotic surgery platforms. Support academic collaborations in related fields. Experience and Abilities Doctoral degree in computer science, electrical and computer engineering, or Master's degree with minimum (5) years industry experience developing computer vision and machine learning applications. Strong understanding and experience in building effective learning systems (data collection, training, evaluation, and making iterative improvements). Strong publication track record in conferences like CVPR, ICCV, MICCAI, etc. Strong hands-on experience with at least one of the mainstream deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch. Strong hands-on experience with Python (proficiency), C/C++ (proficiency), shell scripting Strong engineering practices, debugging/profiling skills, familiarity with multi-threaded programming. Strong hands-on experience with GPU accelerated algorithms and implementations. Strong hands-on experience with state-of-the-art AI models, and generative vision models. Excellent communication skills both written and verbal. Interested in early phases of product exploration and iteration based on incomplete requirements. Solid understanding of computer vision, machine learning, diffusion, and deep learning. Experience with visualization tools is a plus. Self-starter and able to work in a collaborative and results-oriented environment. Ability to travel domestically and internationally (5-15%) Able to view live and recorded surgical procedures.

Under general supervision, the Seal Repair Technician is responsible for all processes related to disassembly and assembly of rotating equipment. The Seal Repair Technician follows instruction from a Repair job packet and router to perform DCI (Dismantle Clean and Inspect) and gives a written description of the wear and condition of critical components seal. This position completes all inspection forms taking pictures of all critical components and uses inspection equipment for proper documentation of the assembly. With assistance identifies, inspects and evaluates material returned, determines repair operations, performs simple shop operations, verify specifications, initiate work and purchase orders. Receives John Crane parts and materials returned by customers and branch offices. Experience in mechanical assembly positions Experience with mechanical seals is a plus

Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.

The Specialist manages the graphics production lifecycle — from concept through live delivery — while collaborating closely with producers, directors, and technical teams. This position plays a key role in maintaining broadcast standards, improving workflows, troubleshooting live graphics issues, and contributing to innovation in augmented reality (AR), virtual reality production VR, and data-driven graphics. Graphics Design & Development Create and customize templates and animations for live broadcasts, including lower thirds, over-the-shoulder graphics, data visualizations, touchscreen graphics, and virtual/augmented reality elements Develop and deploy graphics using real-time rendering engines such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or HTML-based systems Plan, build, maintain, and update graphic directories and playout systems for studio and event workflows Translate creative direction into compelling design, animation, and layout solutions Optimize graphics for performance, stability, and compliance with broadcast standards Prepare and manage image files and assets for production use Ensure visual consistency and adherence to brand standards 2. Workflow Management & Process Optimization Manage the full graphics production pipeline from concept to on-air execution Organize and maintain a centralized graphics asset library with proper version control and archiving Establish, document, and improve efficient workflows and best practices Track and report on project deliverables and performance metrics Assist with hardware/software upgrades and studio builds 3. Collaboration & Live Production Support Collaborate with producers, directors, show teams, and technical staff to meet project goals Serve as a primary contact for troubleshooting real-time graphics issues during live broadcasts Support graphics playout in live event and studio environments Work closely with production teams to design graphics tailored to specific programs or segments Communicate clearly with to manage expectations and ensure timely delivery Independently research and resolve technical challenges 4. Innovation & Industry Advancement Stay current with emerging technologies in real-time graphics and broadcast production Explore opportunities in AR, VR, virtual studios, and data-driven storytelling Contribute innovative ideas that elevate production value and visual storytelling Continuously expand technical skillsets and share knowledge with peers Basic Qualifications Minimum 5+ years of professional experience in real-time television graphics with a strong portfolio/demo reel Advanced expertise in platforms such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or similar systems Strong understanding of broadcast standards, live production workflows, and playout systems Advanced 2D and 3D animation skills with strong typography and layout abilities Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills under live broadcast pressure Strong organizational and communication skills Ability to work flexible hours in live production environments Desired Characteristics: 8+ years of live broadcast graphics experience Familiarity with AR/VR workflows and virtual production tools Knowledge of 3D modeling and animation tools such as Cinema 4D, Blender, or Maya Experience implementing hardware/software upgrades or new studio builds Education Required: High School Diploma or equivalent Preferred: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in design, animation, broadcast technology, or related field Work Environment In-office requirement: four days per week Must be able to work flexible schedules, including evenings and weekends

Position Purpose: Installs and repairs all electrical work throughout the treatment distribution system. Performs electrical work to maintain, install, repair or alter electrical systems found in treatment and pumping facilities, including electrical construction, installation, maintenance, and repair. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment to determine the nature of the problem, repair small and large electrical appliances, repair electronic components of electrical equipment as required for continued operations, make emergency electrical repairs to generators and pumps, and perform related duties as required; and perform related duties as assigned. Perform electrical work to maintain, install or repair all electrical systems, facilities and pump stations. Repair or replace defective or worn electrical parts, components and controlling software in electrical systems and devices, electrical motors, generators, pumps, controllers, lighting systems, and other fixtures and equipment. Work independently and make sound decisions regarding work methods and tools; read, interpret, apply, and enforce applicable codes and standards as related to electrical installation; apply State, Federal, and local safety regulations and codes to electrical work. Work safely both independently and as a crew member on high voltages up to 600 volts AC; work safely near energized primary and secondary lines with voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Read and works from electrical blueprints and drawings. Comprehend and make inferences from written material; read and interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and work orders. Perform preventative maintenance on electrical systems, motors and equipment. Inspect newly installed electrical equipment and lighting to ensure safe operation as well as code compliance. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. This employee can work in high voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Education/Experience/Background: High School Diploma/GED is required. 5 years journey level electrical experience required. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Knowledge of methods, materials, tools, equipment, and procedures used in the installation, maintenance, repair, replacement and alteration of electrical equipment; components and parts used in modern electrical wiring systems such as pumps, motors, controls and lighting. Basic understanding of overhead line construction, Nation Electric Code and Federal and State OSHA standards. Read, interpret and enforce applicable State and Federal codes and requirements. Ability to communicate with all levels including team, management, clients, and vendors in a professional manner both orally and in writing. Safety procedures in electrical maintenance and operations. The employee must be able to operate electric motors fueled by gasoline, diesel, or gaseous fuels, paint, welding, and fabrication equipment, and other hand tools required. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Valid industrial electrician’s license preferred. Physical Requirements: The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, climb stairs or ladders, sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and taste or smell. THE POSITION: Medical Information is a critically important customer-facing function that supports the safe and effective use of pharmaceutical company products by providing timely, scientifically balanced, evidence based, nonpromotional information in response to unsolicited requests from healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and payers. Medical Information also plays an important role in post-marketing handling of adverse events and product complaints. As part of the Medical Information Contact Center (MICC) team, this position delivers industry-leading services, which include Contact Center staffing for responding to product information requests, identifying and handling of adverse events and/or product quality issues, and medical writing as needed to generate written response for use in response to medical questions received. This position requires clinical and therapeutic knowledge, critical and analytical thinking, and customer/patient-centric approach. Medical Information Specialists typically support multiple pharmaceutical clients, multiple products, and multiple therapeutic areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by: MEDICAL INFORMATION SUPPORT Respond to medical information inquiries from physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other health care professionals, consumers, and payers. Utilize medical information skills to identify, research, and critically evaluate medical literature to create responses to medical information inquiries. Utilize writing skills for adverse event and product complaint narrative during intake as well as medical inquiry custom responses. Handle requests across multiple channels and platforms (phone, email, CRM, chat, etc.) Identify adverse events and product complaints during interactions with customers. Perform intake sufficient to generate adverse event and product complaint reports in compliance with EVERSANA-MICC and client standard operating procedures. Knowledge of FDA’s postmarketing adverse event reporting regulations and safety terminology. Ability to make accurate assessments regarding what information needs to be obtained and level or depth of information to be collected. Coordinate processes necessary for responding to product quality-related complaints. This process may involve interactions with personnel in the following departments: Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and the complainant. Maintain product, therapeutic area, and client specific requirements knowledge. Ensure good documentation, high quality, and excellent customer service. Medical writing and Medical Information content development. Provide medical writing to assist in drafting of Medical Information response documents [FAQs, Scientific Response Documents (SRDs), Custom Response Documents (CRDs)] and/or work collaboratively with medical writing team to develop these materials.  Staffing at scientific medical affairs booths. On-call responsibilities on an as assigned basis. Miscellaneous projects such as market and competitive product research, operational and process improvements, field team training and field liaison support.  All other duties as assigned. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. Purpose The Assistant Controller oversees financial accounting, financial reporting, cost allocation, collection of data, and preparation of reports that maintain AbbVie’s cost accounting systems for businesses supported. The Assistant Controller is responsible for maintaining a control environment complaint with internal control policies/procedures to assure accurate financial reporting and responsible commitment of asset/expense resources. The Assistant Controller is a leader in both the Finance Organization as well as the Site Operations and is expected to foster an inclusive and welcoming working environment. Responsibilities Provides guidance and analysis for the various forecasting and reporting cycles (month-end actual reporting, LBE forecasting, LRP and Plan development) ensuring accurate financial results/forecasts for all stakeholders. Oversees and provides guidance for the annual standards setting process including summarizing impact of cost change and presenting results to site leadership teams and region managements.. Partners with site & finance leadership providing financial impact of business decisions, operational reviews and identifying opportunities for cost improvement. Leads and supports business case development for capital investments, sourcing alternatives, third party manufacturing arrangements. Presents findings and recommendations to site and region leadership. Direct management and development of up to 1 staff member with indirect management of other team members. Maintains a robust internal control environment in compliance with AbbVie policies, guidance and regulations. Supports and provides guidance for all plant audits, both internal and external. Supports standard and ad-hoc requests from AbbVie Finance. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance. CPA preferred. 6+ years of experience in finance/accounting required. 2+ years in a manufacturing environment required. Familiarity with standard cost variance analysis required. Strong analytical, problem solving, and communication skills. Must be able to manage multiple priorities and achieve required timelines. Knowledge and proficiency in systems, particularly MS Excel and SAP, is critical. Experience with SAP costing required. Previous supervisory experience preferred.

In support of BSG Creative Account Team, the Account Executive (AE) work with internal staff and external resources to deliver creative and communications solutions that is both cost-effective and high quality. In the AE role you will work independently with clients to execute marketing communications projects. The Account Executive will follow client direction, create estimates, secure resources, and manages timelines and budgets to meet client expectations. The Account Executive’s clients will be various AbbVie employees from all facets of the corporation. With the support of your manager it will be your responsibility to estimate, quote and invoice projects monthly. Meet or exceed financial goal within the role of $110M annually. Positively influence the improvements in process. As an active member of the BD team, share best practices. Provide support outside your ‘normal’ client base, as business may demand. Partner with your manager to strategize on ways to improve effectiveness. Comply with applicable Corporate Policies, Procedures and Mandatory Training. In the spirit of All for One AbbVie, it is our expectation that you have the courage to communicate project, budgetary, resource or quality challenges and concerns openly with your manager. The Account Executive should have the ability to adapt to changing external influences. The ability to build relationships quickly will be an asset to your success in this role. Bachelors Degree: Emphasis in Communication, Marketing, Advertising or Business 2-5 years Project Management/Account Executive in a creative agency, or meeting/event planning environment experience Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Preferred: Working knowledge of InDesign is a plus.
